document: In the Pages panel, open the master (parent) page and move its items onto the document pages, or delete them.

checks.title: Items on a master page
checks.why: Frontify only reads items on the document pages, so anything on a master page (called a parent page in newer InDesign versions) is ignored or breaks the template.

text_frame: Select the text (or the whole frame) and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).

checks.title: Text without a paragraph style
checks.why: Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited. Text set to [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style] has nothing to follow.

font: Make sure the font is installed or activated on your computer.
Package again with File > Package with "Copy Fonts" checked, and zip the whole folder, including "Document fonts".

checks.title: Font missing from the package
checks.why: Frontify needs the font files to render the text, otherwise the template falls back to another font.

font: Get an OTF or TTF version from the font vendor and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.

checks.title: Unsupported font format
checks.why: Frontify can only use OpenType (.otf) and TrueType (.ttf) fonts. Other formats, such as Type 1, can’t be loaded.

font: Install the static (non-variable) version of the font and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.

checks.title: Variable font used
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t support variable fonts, so text using them won’t render correctly.

image: Relink any missing images in Window > Links.
Package again with File > Package with "Copy Linked Graphics" checked.

checks.title: Linked image missing from the package
checks.why: The document links to an image that isn’t in the package, so Frontify can’t show it.

image: In Window > Links, select the image and choose Unembed Link from the panel menu.
Save it into the Links folder and package again.

checks.title: Embedded image
checks.why: Frontify needs images as separate linked files and can’t read images embedded in the document.

image: Double-click to select the image inside the frame, then choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
If you need the flipped look, save a flipped copy of the image file instead.
image_frame: Select the image frame and choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
page_item: Select the item and choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).

checks.title: Item is flipped or skewed
checks.why: Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed items, so they’ll look different or break when edited.

text_frame: Click into the table and choose Table > Convert Table to Text, or rebuild it with separate text frames.

checks.title: Table in a text frame
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t support InDesign tables.

document: Save the graphic as a file (for example SVG, PDF or PNG), delete the pasted version and place the file with File > Place.

checks.title: Pasted graphic
checks.why: Graphics pasted straight into InDesign aren’t linked files, so Frontify can’t read them.

text_frame: For each frame, open Object > Text Frame Options > Auto-Size and make the change noted next to it.

checks.title: Auto-size text frame set up incorrectly
checks.why: Frontify grows auto-size frames as people type, and can’t match how these settings resize the frame.

text_frame: Set Columns to 1 in Object > Text Frame Options. Use separate text frames if you need columns.

checks.title: Text frame has columns
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t support multiple columns inside one text frame.

text_frame: Turn on View > Extras > Show Text Threads, then double-click a frame’s out port to break the thread so each frame holds its own text.

checks.title: Threaded (linked) text frames
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t support text flowing from one frame into another.

image: Select the frame and apply [None] or [Basic Graphics Frame] in Window > Styles > Object Styles, then re-apply any formatting you need directly.
text_frame: Select the frame and apply [None] or [Basic Text Frame] in Window > Styles > Object Styles, then re-apply any formatting you need directly.

checks.title: Object style applied
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t apply object styles, so the frame will look different.

paragraph_style: In the paragraph style, go to Indents and Spacing and set Align to Grid to None.

checks.title: Text aligned to the baseline grid
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t use InDesign’s baseline grid, so line spacing will change.

paragraph_style: In the paragraph style, go to Basic Character Formats and set Kerning to Metrics.

checks.title: Kerning isn’t set to Metrics
checks.why: Frontify spaces letters using the font’s own kerning (Metrics). Other settings make text shift when it’s edited.

character_style: In the character style, go to Basic Character Formats and set Kerning to Metrics.

checks.title: Kerning isn’t set to Metrics
checks.why: Frontify spaces letters using the font’s own kerning (Metrics). Other settings make text shift when it’s edited.

page_item: Select the image, shape or group and choose No Text Wrap in Window > Text Wrap.
Then make room for it with the text frame’s size or insets instead.
text_frame: Select the frame and choose No Text Wrap in Window > Text Wrap.

checks.title: Text wrap applied
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t support text wrap, so text won’t flow around objects and will run underneath them.

paragraph_style: In the paragraph style, go to Character Color and set Tint to 100%.

checks.title: Text color tint isn’t 100%
checks.why: Frontify shows text colors at full strength, so tinted text will look darker.

character_style: In the character style, go to Character Color and set Tint to 100%.
To keep the lighter color, make a tint swatch (Swatches panel > New Tint Swatch) and apply that instead.

checks.title: Text color tint isn’t 100%
checks.why: Frontify shows text colors at full strength, so tinted text will look darker.

character_style: Set Position to Normal in the character style (Basic Character Formats) or in the Character panel.
For symbols like ® or ™, use a smaller point size in a character style instead, or a font’s superscript glyphs.

checks.title: Superscript or subscript text
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t support superscript or subscript, so the text shows at full size on the baseline (for example ® or a footnote number).

font: Install a desktop version of the font (OTF or TTF) that you’re licensed to use, and switch the text to it: Type > Find/Change Font, or update the paragraph and character styles.
Package again with "Copy Fonts" checked, and zip the whole folder, including "Document fonts".

checks.title: Adobe Font used
checks.why: Adobe Fonts aren’t supported in Frontify templates (for licensing reasons), so the template falls back to another font.

paragraph_style: In the paragraph style, go to Hyphenation and uncheck Hyphenate.

checks.title: Hyphenation is on
checks.why: Browsers hyphenate differently from InDesign, so lines may break in different places.

text_frame: Click into the text. A + after the style name in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles means it has extra formatting.
To remove it, select the text and click Clear Overrides at the bottom of the Paragraph Styles panel.
To keep the look, update the style to match instead (right-click the style > Redefine Style), or use a character style for single words.

checks.title: Text formatted outside its paragraph style
checks.why: Formatting added by hand on top of a paragraph style (shown as a + next to the style name) may be lost or look different in Frontify.

image: Delete the unused files from the Links folder before zipping the package.

checks.title: Unused images in the package
checks.why: These files aren’t used in the document and only make the package bigger.

document: For a digital template, set bleed to 0 in File > Document Setup > Bleed and Slug. For print templates, bleed is fine.

checks.title: Document has bleed
checks.why: Bleed is added to every export, which is right for print templates but usually unwanted for digital ones.

paragraph_style: In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.

checks.title: Paragraph Composer used
checks.why: The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.

character_style: Set Baseline Shift to 0 pt in the character style (Advanced Character Formats) or in the Character panel.

checks.title: Baseline shift used
checks.why: Frontify doesn’t support baseline shift, so shifted text sits on the baseline.

text_frame: Delete the frame if it isn’t needed.

checks.title: Empty text frame
checks.why: Empty frames are allowed, but are often left over by accident.

image: Reduce the image’s pixel size or file size if it doesn’t need to be this large.

checks.title: Large image
checks.why: Very large images slow down editing and exporting in Frontify.
